combining rRNA-targeted probes and cytoskeletal or organelle-specific stains provides a fast, high-throughput method for linking genetic sequence information with morphological descriptions in uncultivated eucaryotes, including novel protist taxa.

The main takeaway from our work is that

rRNA-targeted whole cell FISH in combination with immunofluorescent stains for cytoskeletal elements can be used to link ssu rRNA sequences to protist morphology, and thus provide taxonomic context for novel protist phylotypes identified by environmental sequencing.

rRNA-targeted probes can be combined with cytoskeletal stains to link sequences to morphological features of protists, and that this method can be used to describe morphological diversity of uncultivated euryarchaeal and eukaryotic microbes in diverse environments.
the use of FISH and immunostaining can help bridge the gap between morphology and genomics, and provide an efficient way to identify and classify uncultivated protist lineages.
